changes.source_excerpt:
1.1 Initially $x_0\in X$. If an update is made from $x_k\in X$, the self-map condition gives $x_{k+1}=G(x_k)\in X$. Induction proves membership of every entered iterate. [given, F1, induction]

2.1 A continuing pass advances its index by one. At index $N$, either the residual test returns or the budget test returns before another update. Thus the entered indices form an initial segment of $0,\ldots,N$, with at most $N+1$ residual evaluations and $N$ updates. Every pass contains finitely many returning primitives, so the procedure terminates with a stated status. This includes $N=0$. [given, F1, step 1.1, induction] ∎
changes.replacement:
1.1 At the initial entered index $0$, the point $x_0$ belongs to $X$, no update has occurred, and the single pass evaluates one residual. [given, F1, base]

1.2 For an entered index $k\le N$, assume the preceding entered indices are exactly $0,\ldots,k-1$, every entered point through $x_k$ lies in $X$, and at most $k$ updates have occurred before pass $k$. [IH]

1.3 If pass $k$ continues, [F1] requires $k<N$ and sets $x_{k+1}=G(x_k)\in X$ by the self-map condition. The next index is $k+1$ and exactly one additional update has occurred. Thus the assertion of step 1.2 holds at the next entered index. A return creates no further index or update. [given, F1, step 1.2, algebra]

2.1 The base and induction step prove membership of every entered iterate and that the entered indices form an initial segment of $0,\ldots,N$. At index $N$, either the residual test returns or the budget test returns before another update. Hence there are at most $N+1$ residual evaluations and $N$ updates. Every pass contains finitely many returning primitives, so the procedure terminates with a stated status, including when $N=0$. [given, F1, step 1.1, step 1.2, step 1.3, discharge-induction] ∎

changes.source_excerpt:
1.1 The initial point lies in $U$. A failed trial returns the current point; an accepted trial becomes the next iterate only after its membership test succeeds. Induction proves membership of all entered iterates. [given, F1, induction]

2.1 The entered indices form an initial segment of $0,\ldots,N$. At $k=N$ the residual or budget branch returns before a correction. Each earlier index permits one correction call and at most one accepted update. Consequently there are at most $N+1$ explicit residual evaluations, $N$ correction calls and $N$ updates. Singular or invalid-trial returns only shorten this execution. The finitely many returning primitives therefore terminate with a stated status, including when $N=0$. [given, F1, step 1.1, induction] ∎

1.3 A continuing pass requires $k<N$. It makes one correction call; a singular correction or invalid trial returns without entering another index. changes.replacement: In all other smooth cases, form the deterministic initial guess $K_i^{(0)}=f(t_j,X_{j,0},u_j)$ after checking that this query is defined. Before calling Newton, check that the entire seed $K^{(0)}$ belongs to the declared open domain of $R_j$, equivalently that every induced stage state lies in $\Omega_x$ and every required control lies in $\Omega_u$. If this check fails, return `stage-domain-failure` with the failing cell and stage index, the partial result record, and no objective candidate. Otherwise call [[alg-finite-budget-newton-for-vector-residuals]] on $R_j$ with that open evaluation domain, tolerance $\tau_s$ and cap $M_s$.
